### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **61** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/runtime.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-extension-field-suffix.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**48** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 693e1003c981789896ef7084109d2e13a7457e67`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/runtime.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-extension-field-suffix.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 693e1003c981789896ef7084109d2e13a7457e67` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9856aae0c042d8629af437e697bff744d72ed416` — the merge of head `d05c186366d671c85a53069bbbde24dff6bad0b7` into base `693e1003c981789896ef7084109d2e13a7457e67`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9856aae0c042d8629af437e697bff744d72ed416 && git checkout 9856aae0c042d8629af437e697bff744d72ed416
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 693e1003c981789896ef7084109d2e13a7457e67 d05c186366d671c85a53069bbbde24dff6bad0b7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 693e1003c981789896ef7084109d2e13a7457e67 && git merge --no-ff d05c186366d671c85a53069bbbde24dff6bad0b7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 693e1003c981789896ef7084109d2e13a7457e67
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 693e1003c981789896ef7084109d2e13a7457e67` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d05c186366d671c85a53069bbbde24dff6bad0b7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/meta-spelling/meta-url-data.generated.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-object-extension-item.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-extension-field-suffix.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (the save, publish, restore, hydration, write-through and delete-heal hunks), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts (`judgeOverrideWrite` and `refusePackagedBaseOverride`, read), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (the `registerApp` extension loop, read), packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts (`narrowObjectsToPackageClosure`, read), packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts (`artifactItemSlot`, read)

Inputs: card #28574 and its four comments; ADR-0146 on `main` (D2, D3, D10); PR #28811 body, 22 files, two comments, and the net diff of head `d05c186366d671c85a53069bbbde24dff6bad0b7` against its merge-base with `origin/main`, `0aaad18fc052326bc78378ead5f7e789f64e072d`; the check-runs on the head. Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no login note is owed.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `MetadataTypeSchema` gains `object_extension` (`metadata-plugin.zod.ts`). Widening of the published enum. Every total record over `MetadataType` is filled in the same diff: `OVERRIDE_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION` (spec) and `KIND_COVERAGE` (showcase). Correct.
2. The registry row: `allowRuntimeCreate: true`, `supportsVersioning: true`, `supportsOverlay: false`, `allowEnvironmentOverlay: false`, `executionPinned: false`, `loadOrder: 11`, `domain: 'data'`, `filePatterns: ['**/*.extension.ts']`. This is the seat's shape A plus the file pattern the registry pin requires. `loadOrder` 11 is unique (object 10, capability 12) and above `object`, as the pin asks. The row's `description` is why the type is a bare type in the translation ledgers (31 to 32 types, 24 to 26 leaves); the counts in the two ledger tests follow from the row. Correct.
3. URL spelling: `object_extensions` and `objectExtensions` both fold to `object_extension`; `REGISTRY_DECLARED_META_TYPES` gains the type after `object`. I compared the hunk with `packages/spec/scripts/build-meta-url-spelling.ts`: the generator emits `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` first, then appends registry-derived spellings in registry order. `object_extensions` and `objectExtensions` land after `books` (the last manifest key) and before `fields` (the next registry-derived key), which is exactly where the hunk puts them. `check:meta-url-spelling` runs in the green Lint lap. Regenerated, not hand-edited.
4. Override classification: `object_extension: excluded / adr_0146_d10_extended`. Read against its consumer `judgeOverrideWrite`: an undeclared body of a non-overridable type answers `not_concerned`, so the pair's save is admitted; a body carrying `overrides` is refused. The disposition does not close the type, and the last test pins that. Correct. See ④ for the refusal sentence.
5. Who may author: the door's own writable-package refusal runs before the gate (a read-only base answers 4xx and leaves no row, pinned). The gate then admits any writable package whose dependency closure holds the target: the pair, or a vendor dependent. ADR-0146 D10 allows both: the pair's fields carry `__c`; a vendor's field on another vendor's object keeps the plain spelling. The `__c` judge is called unchanged and partitions the two cases. Correct.
6. The `__c` field-suffix rule: for a pair, every unsuffixed `fields` key is refused with an issue path at the key (`fields.region` in the pin), and the sentence names `fieldPatches`; for a non-pair, a suffixed key is refused. An extension of the package's own object is not judged. Save, per-item publish, package publish (the shared promotion) and history restore all ask it. Correct.
7. Registration: the whole parsed body (`ObjectExtensionSchema` output, `_provenance: 'org'`) goes through the new `SchemaRegistry.registerObjectExtension`, which calls `registerObject(..., 'extend', priority)`; the `extend` arm replaces the same package's earlier contribution. Boot, write-through and read-side hydration share one method. Withdrawal is the new `withdrawObjectExtension`, keyed on `extend` plus package, and only `'org'`-provenance contributors whose package has no active row left are withdrawn, so a code package's manifest extension of the same object is never touched. Correct. The card named `subtractExtenderContributions`; read, it is the fold's `indexes` idempotency helper, so the dev's substitution is right.
8. The stored-row shape gate: `resolveOverlaySchema` binds `ObjectExtensionSchema`, strict, over the body with the ADR-0010 envelope removed; the type stays out of `BUILTIN_METADATA_TYPE_SCHEMAS`. `reference-sites.ts` walks the type with the same schema, so the `unwalkableSourceTypes` pin stays at `['external_catalog']`. No new error code; the gate uses `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400, the shape gate 422 `INVALID_METADATA`. Correct.
9. Export: `assemblePackageManifest` adds an `objectExtensions` leg and keeps only owned `objects`. Round trip: the exported entry re-parses and `registerApp` registers it as `'extend'` (pinned in a fresh kernel). Card Wanted 5 says `installPackage`; `PackageInstallManifestSchema` is `ManifestSchema.extend({ scope })` with no collection keys, so that door never took any collection. The deviation is recorded in the PR body and is right. The `objects` filter fixes a defect this card makes reachable: an extending package's export carried the target as its own object. Correct.
10. `@objectstack/lint/runtime` re-exports `closureDependencyRemedy`. One line, additive. Correct.
11. `AuthoringGateHost` gains a required member. It is not exported from the package index, so no published interface widens. Correct.
12. Route ledger, SDK and OpenAPI: no generated file outside the three above enumerates the type list; the ledger names types only in one route's prose. "Did not move" holds. The two reference pages regenerate the enum and are prose faces.

### ② Semver level

Minor on `spec`, `lint`, `objectql`, `metadata-protocol`, `runtime`, `platform-objects`. Each is additive: an enum member, a registry row, a classification row, a re-export, two new `SchemaRegistry` methods and one exported function, a new authorable type behind existing doors, a new export collection, new translation leaves. The `objects` filter in the export changes an output, but it removes a row that re-install refused, so no consumer loses a working input. Minor is right.

Declarations: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` stand at line start in the PR body and in `.changeset/28574-object-extension-package-item.md`. They agree with the diff: a published enum widened and a metadata type added.

Check-runs on the head: every run concluded `success` or `skipped`; none failed. No commit statuses. The gate verdicts are green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev cost 1, no JSON schema from `/meta/types` for the type: accepted. It follows from the seat's ruling (no `BUILTIN_METADATA_TYPE_SCHEMAS` entry). Recorded in the body and the changeset.
- Dev cost 2, no `_diagnostics` badge on a draft: accepted, same reason.
- `open_questions[0]`, whether N-23c needs the type bound with the ADR-0010 envelope: answer A for this card. Binding it changes what a manifest's `objectExtensions` parse with, which is a spec ruling the card forbade. N-23c (#28575) raises B if its form cannot be built from the object.
- `open_questions[1]`, whether the adopt-orphans door should judge `object_extension` rows: answer A. The type is new, so no package-less row of it exists, and the gate's first step refuses writing one (pinned).
- Dev flag, `subtractExtenderContributions` is not a withdrawal: confirmed by reading `registry.ts`; the new verb is right.
- Dev flag, `installPackage` refuses every collection key: confirmed by reading `package-api.zod.ts`; the round trip through `registerApp` is the documented install path.
- Dev out-of-scope note, the suffix judge's header omits `os build`: prose, not filed. Agreed.
- Prose drift I found: the registry row's comment says the artifact loader "already stores" a code package's extensions under this type. `artifactItemSlot` stores an item only when it carries `name`; a parsed extension never does (the alias folds `name` into `extend`). So the loader stores none. The PR body's probe also shows `objects: []` where the code omits the key. Both prose; see should-fix 3.

### ④ Design judgment

`customization-package.ts` against ADR-0146 D10 and `judgeOverrideWrite`. D10 says objects are extended, never replaced, and the extension is the `objectExtensions` entry of the pair. An extension is the mechanism, so it has no override channel of its own; `excluded` on the D10 basis is coherent, and no new basis is minted. The consumer reads the row and admits the pair's undeclared save. Holds. One sentence misfits: a body that carries `overrides` on this type is refused as `declared_type_not_overridable` with the D6 text "create your own object_extension under a new name". An extension has no new name; its name is its target. The `declared_object` refusal still points at the manifest entry, not at the item door this PR opens. Both are one-sentence fixes in cited code (should-fix 1).

`metadata-plugin.zod.ts` against D10 and its first consumers. The row makes the type runtime-creatable and versioned, with no overlay; the doors refuse what the ADR refuses (`__c` outside the pair, unsuffixed inside it, a target outside the closure, an unknown target, a row named other than its target, a package-less write, `defaultRowScope` and `membershipKeys`). The one item per package per target shape is carried by the row name, and the body keeps `extend` with no `name`, so a GET round-trips through the strict schema. `loadMetaFromDb` reads active rows in store order, not by `loadOrder`, so the 11 is a declaration of intent rather than a boot ordering. That is harmless: the `extend` arm opens an entry when the owner has not arrived, and the later `own` registration finds no conflicting owner. Holds.

`meta-url-data.generated.ts` against its generator and `canonicalMetaUrlType`. Both spellings fold; the checklist gate reads the declared list. Holds.

Scenarios, each read against the code:
- An extension whose target is outside the written package's closure: step 5 refuses with the closure sentence (pinned for `com.acme.other`). The closure keeps platform objects and package-less rows, which is the conservative direction every save door takes. Holds.
- An extension that redefines a base field: for the pair, an unsuffixed key is refused and the sentence names `fieldPatches` (pinned). For a non-pair dependent, a plain `fields` key equal to the target's own field is spread over it by `mergeObjectDefinitions`. That is the manifest fold as it stands on `main`, and N-23d's target-field check covers `fieldPatches`, not `fields`. Not this PR's change; should-fix 2 names it.
- An extension authored into a read-only base: the door's writable-package refusal answers before the gate (pinned 4xx, no row). The sealed-write refusal cannot fire on this type either: `isSealedManagedItem` needs an artifact of `(object_extension, name)`, and the loader stores none. Holds.
- A field lacking `__c` where the rule requires it: refused at save, publish and restore, with the issue path (pinned, probed). Holds.
- Two packages extending one object with the same field name: the pair and a dependent cannot collide, since `__c` partitions them. Two dependents, or two pairs when one base depends on another, both at default priority 200: `mergeObjectDefinitions` spreads `fields`, so the later-registered contribution wins with no refusal and no report. Pre-existing on the manifest path; the runtime door now reaches it from Studio. Should-fix 2.
- Export, then re-install: the pair's export carries the entry, the base's carries none, and `registerApp` in a fresh kernel registers the same field (pinned). The engine's `registerApp` loop copies a hand list of keys; at this head that list equals the schema's keys (`fields`, `fieldPatches`, `label`, `pluralLabel`, `description`, `validations`, `indexes`, with `extend` and `priority` read separately), so nothing is lost on the round trip today. A key added to `ObjectExtensionSchema` later must be added to that loop too. Observation, no finding.
- Interplay with N-09: an undeclared `object_extension` row is `not_concerned` because the type is not overridable and no artifact of the type exists to collide with; a declared one is refused. Holds, with the sentence note above.
- A short target name that `getObject` folds to a legacy `ns__name` key: the gate would admit it and `registerObject` would open a second entry under the short name. `computeFQN` is the identity today and the manifest loop behaves the same way, so the reach is legacy keys only. Should-fix 4.

Findings:
1. Should-fix. `judgeOverrideWrite`'s two sentences: the `declared_type_not_overridable` text does not fit an extension, and `declared_object` should name the `object_extension` item door beside the manifest entry. Cited code, not this diff; file a small follow-up.
2. Should-fix. No door or registry refusal when two extenders of one object declare the same field name; the fold is last-writer-wins at equal priority. Pre-existing; file a follow-up card under the epic, since the runtime door makes it reachable from Studio.
3. Should-fix. Prose: the registry row's comment claims the artifact loader stores extensions under this type; it does not. The PR body's probe shows `objects: []` where the code omits the key. Fix at next touch.
4. Should-fix. The gate could pin `extend` to the key `getObject` resolved, refusing a spelling that differs, so an admitted row can never land on a phantom entry. Legacy reach only.

No must-fix.
